result.title: Asking the right question is key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses
result.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) scientists pursue discovery through a chain of hypotheses, fitting candidate models to existing observations and often choosing experiments where those models disagree most. Yet when early data miss a narrow feature, model selection favors simple curves that agree across the unmea- sured gap, so disagreement-guided search has no reason to look where the new phenomenon lies. When we tested two frontier AI scientists, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, across 32 closed-loop trials with a narrow peak omitted from the starting data, both sampled inside the peak region less often than random search. Surprisingly, the agent that followed model disagreement more closely missed the peak in all 32 trials, whereas discovery succeeded when experiments probed the unmeasured gap early and followed up across the anomaly. Asking the right question, rather than testing only where current models disagree, is therefore key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses.

AI.brief_summary: 该文让两个前沿 AI scientist 在 32 个闭环试验中从遗漏窄峰的数据出发做假设链式发现，发现按模型分歧选实验的智能体反而不如随机搜索，甚至全部错过窄峰；只有早期探测未测量区间并追踪异常才成功。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是与视觉无关的假设—实验选择研究，但其「分歧引导探索失效、需主动探测信息空白」的负结果，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据获取与筛选策略提供问题表述层面的启发，可供核查标题为「Asking the right question」的原文实验设定与探索准则。
